front.label: Front addition
front.title: A modern warm-white front.
front.text: Smooth warm-white stucco wraps the front walls, gables, bay base and corner returns, under a charcoal standing-seam roof with charcoal fascia. The window frames are white, with white grid bars dividing the glass of the bay and of the high window over the entrance. Warm vertical wood cladding lines the recessed entry around the walnut front door, and a stained-cedar carriage-house garage door with a top row of glass lites, flanked by black coach lanterns, completes the front. Bedroom 3 keeps its tall bay window and a solid gable above it. The rectangular high window over the entrance, the vaulted front bedroom and the coordinated rooflines are retained. Roof forms are inferred from your aerial photo; dimensions remain proposed.

B3.label: Bedroom 3
B3.title: A canted bay glazed to the floor.
B3.text: White frames with white grid bars run from the floor to the 7′6″ head, three lites wide and five high in the centre sash and two wide and five high in each side sash, so the bay reads as part of the room and opens it to the front garden. The floor extends into the bay. The bed sits on the west wall to keep it open. Bay: 8′ wall opening, 2′ projection, glazed to the floor. Above the bay is a continuous plaster gable, and the vaulted ceiling rises to 11′6″ at the ridge, lit by a ring pendant. The bathroom and compact closet remain on the opposite wall, with the hall entrance at the side. The foyer wall lines up with the shared bathroom's wall, so the room is 14′10⅜″ wide.

B4.label: Bedroom 4
B4.title: Bedroom 4: a flat ceiling and the bed turned across the room.
B4.text: A calm flat ceiling replaces the vault, at the same 8 ft as the rest of the house. The full bed is turned across the room, with its headboard on the north wall and its side along the window wall, so the room's length stays open from the bed to the door and the reach-in closet. The desk stands in a niche on the north wall, between the nightstand and the back wall of the laundry closet, which takes the room's north-east corner and opens onto the foyer. The room (the architect's office), its separate reach-in closet and the west-facing window keep their positions; overall the room is still 8′0″ deep as on the architect's plan and 14′10⅜″ wide, because its foyer wall lines up with the shared bathroom's wall, and it is now L-shaped around the laundry closet.

K0.label: Kitchen
K0.title: A warm vintage kitchen in cream, oak and brass.
K0.text: Cream shaker cabinets with unlacquered brass cup pulls and knobs, glass-front uppers and a greige tall-cabinet wall at the hall end, where a stainless-steel French-door refrigerator with a bottom freezer drawer stands right beside a built-in microwave over the stainless wall oven. A cream plaster hood with a dentil band rises over a scalloped marble backsplash and a brass pot filler, beside walnut open shelves on whitewashed brick. The fireclay farmhouse sink sits under the white grid window, three sashes of two by four lites in a white casing, with brass sconces and linen café curtains. Amber-glass pendants hang over a white-oak island with a thick grey-veined quartzite top and a Persian runner, and a warm oak dining table for six continues the island's west end, toward the hall, under a brass lantern, so the floor between the island and the family room stays open. A 3′6″ × 4′ skylight sits on the continuous east roof plane, over the sink and dishwasher. Proposed window: 6′ wide, 3′1¾″ sill, 7′9″ head. Styled after your kitchen style images.

A0.label: Primary bathroom
A0.title: A white primary bath with one wall of stacked stone.
A0.text: The room is white, with one feature wall. Natural stacked stone in warm browns runs the full width and height of the vanity wall, the south wall, behind the floating solid-oak slab with its two basins carved into the wood. Two oak-framed mirrors hang on the stone under a rough dark timber beam, with an enamel-shade lamp over each basin, and a second beam crosses the ceiling. Every other wall is plain white from the floor to the ceiling, above a white tile base and under a white ceiling, and the floor is quiet grey stone. The curbless shower in the north-west corner stands behind frameless glass under the 2′0″ × 2′6″ skylight, lined in matte white tile, with a brushed-nickel rain shower. The room follows the architect's sheet: the toilet is in the south-west corner, the 6′6″ double vanity runs along the south wall, and the door is at the east end of the north wall, off the suite's vestibule and next to the walk-in closet, which is a room of its own behind a sliding pocket door. The west window is 3′0″ wide, from a 2′0″ sill to the ceiling, in a white frame with white grid bars below its transom and a linen roman shade on the sash outside the shower. The stone wall, the oak and the timber follow your primary bathroom wall style image.

A1.label: Shared bathroom
A1.title: A wood-look wall and warm stone in the shared bath.
A1.text: A rustic oak wood-look tile wall rises behind the wall-hung toilet and around a softly lit, wood-lined niche, with warm Spanish-cream stone-look porcelain on the other walls. A floating light-oak vanity carries a honed travertine block with a carved trough basin, a wall-mounted brushed-nickel faucet and a backlit mirror. The floor is light limestone-look tile, and the alcove tub keeps its glass screen and lit niche. The existing tub, vanity, toilet orientation and room footprint remain. Styled after your shared bathroom style images.

roof.label: Roof connections
roof.title: Roof planes meet at defined ridges and sloped valleys.
roof.text: The broad main hip and front garage gable follow the forms visible in IMG_3202.PNG. The new 6:12 bedroom gable continues over Bedrooms 3 and 4. A small drainage cricket at the rear hip connection removes a level trough and directs water into sloped valleys. A lower entry gable has a slight fall toward the front so the side valleys are not level. The entry clerestory is coordinated to 3′ × 2′3″. Main and garage 4:12 pitches are provisional. The roof is shown in charcoal standing-seam metal. This is a concept roof model; field measurements, framing and drainage detailing remain to be resolved.

LC.label: Laundry closet
LC.title: A stacked washer and dryer off the foyer, next to Bedroom 4.
LC.text: The laundry closet is carved out of Bedroom 4's north-east corner and opens onto the foyer, on its west side right next to the bedroom door. A front-load washer with the dryer stacked on top stands centred behind a pair of narrow doors in a 2′6″ × 6′8″ opening; the doors are hinged on the two jambs and shown wide open against the foyer wall. The closet is 2′10″ wide and 3′0″ deep inside, under the 8 ft ceiling; the oak floor runs in from the foyer, a recessed outlet box and the dryer vent are on the back wall, and a flush light sits in the ceiling. Bedroom 4 keeps its overall size and is L-shaped around the closet. The units are generic models of a typical stacked pair (27″ wide, 30¼″ deep, 39″ high each), not a selected product: connections, vent route and clearances need to be confirmed for the appliances you choose.

changes: Bedroom 4 (plan: office): flat 8 ft ceiling instead of the vault
Front bedroom bay (tour: Bedroom 3, plan: Bedroom #2): glazed down to the floor; window seat removed
Foyer: two skylights on the entry roof's east slope (hall section and vaulted entry)
Primary bedroom: the 7 ft rear window becomes a two-panel sliding door to the garden (landing outside)
Bedroom 2 (next to the primary): rear window runs to the ceiling (sill 2'-0" since the third round)

Primary bathroom: tall west window in clear glass, sill 2'-0" since the third round (an evergreen screen in the fenced side yard outside). It stood between the vanity and the shower of the earlier layout; the sixth round moves it to the architect's position and widens it to 3'-0"
Kitchen skylight: 3'-6" x 4'-0" on the continuous east roof plane over the sink / dishwasher (the concept unit straddled the garage-gable ridge)
Dining: table in line with the island, no island stools (warm oak under a brass lantern since the third round; moved to the island's west end, 6'-0" x 2'-9" for six, in the fifth round)
Primary bathroom: a 2'-0" x 2'-6" skylight over the shower (in the sixth round it moves with the shower to the room's north-west corner)

The foyer-side wall of Bedroom 4 (office) and Bedroom 3 lines up with the shared bath's east wall: both rooms and the closets between them are 1'-2 3/4" wider; foyer and covered porch 5'-9 1/4" wide; foyer 18'-6" long as on the plan; the 3'-0" front door stays centred
Rear landing outside the living room sized as on the plan (3'-0" deep, garden door to x 38'-3")
Bedroom 2 rear window and the primary bathroom window: a 2'-0" sill instead of glass to the floor (heads stay at the 8 ft ceiling)
Bedroom 4: the bed is turned across the room, headboard on the north wall, so the room's length stays open

Kitchen, primary bathroom, shared bathroom and garage door restyled from the owner's style images (styles/); the primary bathroom's finishes of this round (green shower tile, patterned floor) are superseded by the sixth round, the oak trough vanity stays; the kitchen's black steel grid window and its refrigerator behind cabinet panels are superseded by the seventh round (a white grid window, a visible stainless-steel refrigerator)

Laundry closet with a stacked front-load washer and dryer behind a 2'-6" x 6'-8" door opening. It was first built in the kitchen's south-west corner, where the architect's sheet SKA002 draws "W / D": superseded by the fifth round, which moves it to Bedroom 4
Kitchen south wall re-planned around that closet (closet, refrigerator, wall ovens, a short counter, the cooktop): superseded by the fifth round, the wall is back to its third-round layout

Laundry closet moved out of the kitchen: it is carved out of Bedroom 4's north-east corner and opens east onto the foyer, on the foyer's west side next to the bedroom door. 2'-10" wide x 3'-0" deep clear, the stacked front-load washer and dryer behind a pair of doors in a 2'-6" x 6'-8" opening, shown open

Bedroom 4 is L-shaped after the cut: 14'-10 3/8" x 8'-0" overall as before, less 3'-4 3/8" x 3'-2 1/4" for the closet and its two walls (108.2 sq ft); the desk stands in the niche between the nightstand and the closet's back wall

Dining table moved from the family-room side of the island to the island's west end, the shared-bathroom side, in line with the island: 6'-0" x 2'-9", three chairs on each long side, none at the ends, no rug; the floor between the island and the family room is open

Kitchen south wall back to its third-round layout: refrigerator and oven tower at the west (hall) end, then the counter under three glass-front uppers and the cooktop under the hood (until the seventh round the refrigerator stood behind cabinet panels and the tower held two wall ovens)

Front bedroom suite bathroom (tour: Bedroom 3 bathroom): the window in the shower is vertically larger, from a 3'-0" sill to a 7'-6" head (4'-6" tall; it was 2'-0" tall above a 5'-0" sill). Its 3'-0" width and the obscured glass stay (the frame, black in this round, is white with grid bars since the seventh)

Primary walk-in closet: a small room with a door, as on the last page of sizes.pdf (sheet SKA002). 6'-1" x 8'-0" clear behind a new wall, entered from the suite's vestibule through a sliding pocket door (2'-6" x 6'-8", the leaf slides south into the wall, shown open), with hanging rods and shelves on three sides. The open dressing area with its wardrobes is gone

Primary suite as on the sheet: a vestibule between the closet and the hall, 4'-7" x 8'-0" clear, open to the bedroom over its full width (no door), with the attic access hatch in its ceiling. The suite entry from the hall is a 2'-8" opening with a sliding panel on the hall side, shown open; it stands 1'-8" south of its place on the sheet, where this model has Bedroom 2's entry alcove on the hall side

Primary bedroom as on the sheet: king bed on the west wall, centred between the two west windows, with a nightstand on each side; both west windows are kept (the sheet draws only the north one), and so is the rear sliding door

Primary bathroom laid out as on the sheet: a 5'-0" x 3'-0" curbless shower in the north-west corner, the toilet in the south-west corner, a 6'-6" double vanity along the south wall, the door at the east end of the north wall. The west window is at the sheet's position, 3'-0" wide from the 2'-0" sill to the ceiling, its mullion on the shower's glass line, and the 2'-0" x 2'-6" skylight moved with the shower

Primary bathroom in the style of the owner's image "primary bathroom wall style" (styles/): natural stacked stone on the vanity wall, behind the floating oak vanity with its two wooden troughs and the oak-framed mirrors, under a dark timber beam with enamel lamps; a quiet grey stone floor; brushed nickel fittings. The green shower tile and the blue patterned floor are gone. The grey-green board wainscot with cream plaster above it on the other walls and the cream shower tile of this round are superseded by the seventh round (white walls, white tile)

Refrigerator next to the microwave: the refrigerator stood behind cabinet panels and read as a pantry. It is now a visible stainless-steel French-door refrigerator with a bottom freezer drawer, in the same bay at the hall end of the kitchen's tall wall, under a two-door cabinet. The unit directly beside it, above the wall oven, is a built-in microwave (it was a second wall oven). Nothing else in the kitchen changes

All windows white, with grid lines: every window frame, sash, mullion and transom bar is white, inside and outside, and every window and glazed door has white grid bars (7/8 in wide, on both faces of the glass) with lites as near 14 x 16 1/2 in as each sash allows, the bars in line across sashes and transoms. That includes the primary bedroom's sliding door, the living room's rear glazing and garden door, the bay, the tall windows of Bedroom 2 and the primary bathroom, the obscured bathroom window, the window above the front door and the kitchen window, which was a black steel grid window and keeps its 2 x 4 lites per sash, now white. The skylights, the shower glass, the garage door and the front door are as they were, shades and curtains stay in front of the grids, and no window opening changes its place or size

Primary bathroom walls coherent and white: the grey-green board wainscot, its cap rail and the cream plaster are removed. Every wall except the vanity wall is plain white from the floor to the ceiling, above a white tile base; the ceiling is white and the shower tile is matte white (it was cream). The stacked stone on the vanity wall stays as the one feature wall, with the timber beams, the oak vanity and mirrors, the lamps, the shelf, the grey stone floor, the fittings and the layout

Fireplace sealed, sofa on that side, television opposite: the living room's fireplace is removed with its stone surround, firebox and hearth ledge, and the east wall is a plain white wall with its baseboard; the east windows are untouched. The sofa stands against that wall, facing west, with a side table and a lamp at each end, a round rug and a round coffee table in front of it and an armchair to the north-west, as the architect's sheet draws it. A 75 in television hangs on the opposite wall, the west wall shared with Bedroom 2, centred on the sofa, over a low oak media console. The way from the dining area to the rear glass and the garden door stays open

Daylight corrected for the yard, which faces north: the sun was already in the south-east (late morning), but the sky was turned half a circle, with its bright side over the garden. The sky's glow now stands at the sun, over the street side, and its deep-blue side over the garden. The rear of the house, the deck by the house and the near lawn are in the house's shade; no direct sun comes in through the north-facing glass (the primary bedroom's sliding door, Bedroom 2's rear window, the living room's rear glazing), and sun patches fall only through the east windows, the front bay, the window above the front door and the skylights

Exterior: the redesign of the exterior that the owner raised with this round was set aside by the owner. Roof, massing, entry and facade are as they were; only the white window frames and grid bars show outside
